notes: Khozyain becomes 'owner', which works for both a business and a dog, as the adaptNote says. The thug is the boss puppet as a gangster with a gold chain; he walks in on the narrator line.
title: The Owner

lines.text: A thuggish hulk with a massive chain around his neck walks into the office. He goes up to the guard and asks, looking down at him:
Where's the owner?
Lost your owner? Bark.

notes: Khozyain becomes 'Besitzer', which fits a business and a dog; the guard repeats the same word so the dog image lands. The thug is the boss puppet as a gangster with a gold chain.
title: Der Besitzer

lines.text: Ins Büro kommt ein bulliger Kerl mit einer dicken Kette um den Hals. Er geht zum Wachmann und fragt von oben herab:
Wo ist der Besitzer?
Besitzer verloren? Dann bell mal.

notes: Source wording kept; the stage direction about patting the head became a short narrator line in the source's words. Both new Russians wear gold chains and crimson; the other's huge guard stands next to him, the frail decoy (paren in a dark suit) next to his boss.
title: Четвёртый охранник

lines.text: Встреча новых русских. Каждый привёл с собой громадину-охранника. И только у одного — щуплый, низкорослый, болезненного вида.
Он у тебя крутой боец?
Да нет, совсем никакой.
Снайпер?
Никогда оружия в руках не держал.
Так зачем ты его за собой таскаешь?
Поглаживая охранника по голове:
А он у меня уже четвёртый такой, все его за меня принимают.

notes: Translated line by line; the head-patting stage direction is a short narrator line. Both New Russians wear gold chains and crimson; the other's huge guard and the frail decoy (paren in a dark suit) are on screen.
title: The Fourth Bodyguard

lines.text: A meeting of New Russians. Each one has brought a huge bodyguard. Only one has a puny, short, sickly-looking one.
Is he some tough fighter?
No, not at all.
A sniper?
Never held a gun in his life.
So why do you drag him around with you?
Patting the bodyguard on the head:
He's already my fourth one like this. Everyone takes him for me.

notes: Translated line by line; the head-patting stage direction is a short narrator line. Both neue Russen wear gold chains and crimson; the other's huge guard and the frail decoy (paren in a dark suit) are on screen.
title: Der vierte Leibwächter

lines.text: Ein Treffen neuer Russen. Jeder hat einen riesigen Leibwächter mitgebracht. Nur einer hat einen schmächtigen, kleinen, kränklich aussehenden.
Ist er ein harter Kämpfer?
Ach was, überhaupt nicht.
Ein Scharfschütze?
Hatte noch nie eine Waffe in der Hand.
Wozu schleppst du ihn dann überall mit?
Er tätschelt dem Leibwächter den Kopf:
Er ist schon mein vierter von der Sorte. Alle halten ihn für mich.

notes: Source wording kept. Cross-cut: the man comes home and reads the pager (phone prop), the mistress with red lipstick voices her message, then the wife stands next to him for the second message.
title: Пейджер

lines.text: Мужик оставил дома пейджер, вечером возвращается, читает сообщения. Первое:
Милый, дорогой, любимый, позвони мне, пожалуйста. Целую, всегда твоя Марина.
Второе:
Я уже позвонила, можешь не беспокоиться. Твоя жена.

notes: Pager became a phone (adaptNote); the mistress signs with the puppet's English name. Cross-cut: the man reads at home, the mistress voices her message, then the wife stands next to him for the second one.
title: Two Messages

lines.text: A man left his phone at home. In the evening he comes back and reads his messages. The first one:
Honey, darling, my love, please call me. Kisses, forever yours, Jessica.
The second one:
I've already called her, you needn't bother. Your wife.

notes: Pager became a Handy (adaptNote); the mistress signs with the puppet's German name. Cross-cut: the man reads at home, the mistress voices her message, then the wife stands next to him for the second one.
title: Zwei Nachrichten

lines.text: Ein Mann hat sein Handy zu Hause vergessen. Abends kommt er zurück und liest die Nachrichten. Die erste:
Liebling, Schatz, mein Süßer, ruf mich bitte an. Küsschen, für immer deine Jenny.
Die zweite:
Ich habe sie schon angerufen, du brauchst dich nicht zu bemühen. Deine Frau.

notes: Source wording kept, numbers as words, speech tags cut; Stirlitz says his closing thought himself. The contact is visible from the start as a drunk with a bottle on the left stool, so the punchline pays off on screen.
title: Штирлиц в баре

lines.text: Штирлиц пришёл на встречу со связным в знакомый бар и заказал сто грамм водки.
Водка у нас кончилась ещё два дня назад.
Ну, тогда сто грамм коньячку.
Коньячок у нас кончился вчера.
Ну, а пиво-то есть?
Увы, закончилось сегодня утром.
Значит, связной уже здесь.

notes: Stirlitz introduced as a Soviet spy (adaptNote); a hundred grams became a double. Speech tags cut; he says his closing thought himself. The contact is visible as a drunk with a bottle on the left stool.
title: Stirlitz at the Bar

lines.text: Stirlitz, the Soviet spy, came to a familiar bar to meet his contact and ordered a double vodka.
Sorry, we ran out of vodka two days ago.
Well, a double cognac then.
The cognac ran out yesterday.
Well, you've got beer, at least?
I'm afraid that ran out this morning.
So my contact is already here.

notes: Stirlitz introduced as a Soviet spy (adaptNote); a hundred grams became a Doppelter. Speech tags cut; he says his closing thought himself. The contact is visible as a drunk with a bottle on the left stool.
title: Stirlitz in der Kneipe

lines.text: Stirlitz, der sowjetische Spion, kam in eine vertraute Kneipe, um seinen Verbindungsmann zu treffen, und bestellte einen doppelten Wodka.
Der Wodka ist uns leider schon vor zwei Tagen ausgegangen.
Na, dann einen doppelten Cognac.
Der Cognac ist gestern ausgegangen.
Na, aber Bier habt ihr doch?
Leider seit heute Morgen alle.
Also ist mein Verbindungsmann schon da.

notes: Source wording kept. The opening narration is shown instead of told: the wife puts the phone down, the husband sits on the sofa behind a newspaper.
title: Звонок мамы

lines.text: Это кто был?
Да мама. Она, по-моему, уже наполовину сумасшедшая.
А-а-а... Значит, получше стало.

notes: Translated line by line. The opening narration is shown instead of told: the wife puts the phone down, the husband sits on the sofa behind a newspaper.
title: Mom Called

lines.text: Who was that?
Oh, Mom. I think she's already half crazy.
Ah... So she's getting better.

notes: Translated line by line. The opening narration is shown instead of told: the wife puts the phone down, the husband sits on the sofa behind a newspaper.
title: Mama hat angerufen

lines.text: Wer war das?
Ach, Mama. Ich glaube, sie ist schon halb verrückt.
Aha... Dann geht's ihr also besser.

notes: Source wording kept. Two friends: the curious one is muzhik, the sad young man with the girlfriend is paren; the girlfriend is only mentioned in his story.
title: Имя на стекле

lines.text: Встречаются два приятеля. Один в плохом настроении.
Ты чего такой грустный?
Да с девушкой своей поссорился.
Из-за чего?
Ехали мы с ней вчера в метро, и я всю дорогу дышал на стекло и писал её имя, а она обиделась.
Странно! Разве на это можно обидеться?
Да не любит она, когда ей на очки дышат.

notes: Translated line by line; 'the glass' and 'her glasses' keep the reveal even tighter in English. Curious friend muzhik, sad boyfriend paren.
title: Name on the Glass

lines.text: Two friends meet. One of them is in a bad mood.
Why so glum?
I had a fight with my girlfriend.
What about?
We were riding the subway yesterday, and the whole way I kept breathing on the glass and writing her name, and she got offended.
Weird! How can anyone be offended by that?
Well, she doesn't like it when you breathe on her glasses.

notes: Translated line by line; 'aufs Glas' and 'auf die Brille' keep the reveal. Curious friend muzhik, sad boyfriend paren.
title: Name auf dem Glas

lines.text: Zwei Kumpel treffen sich. Einer ist schlecht gelaunt.
Warum bist du so traurig?
Hab mich mit meiner Freundin gestritten.
Weswegen?
Wir sind gestern mit der U-Bahn gefahren, und ich hab die ganze Fahrt aufs Glas gehaucht und ihren Namen geschrieben, und sie war beleidigt.
Komisch! Wie kann man denn deswegen beleidigt sein?
Na, sie mag es nicht, wenn man ihr auf die Brille haucht.

notes: Source wording kept; the wife's reported order became her line, speech tag cut. Three scenes: home, the forest where the cat walks off and the man stays lost, home again where the cat and then the unshaven man walk in. 'на хрен' softened to 'нафиг'.
title: Кот в лесу

lines.text: У одного мужика был кот. И то ли старый котяра уже стал, то ли сметану спёр, но жена мужика приказала:
Отнеси его далеко в лес и оставь там на произвол судьбы!
Делать нечего — понёс мужик кота в лес.
И сам пропал.
День его нет, два нет, на третий день появляется дома кот,
и тут же мужик следом — грязный, злой и голодный.
Ну ты чего, урод, отнёс кота в лес?
Ага, отнёс, блин! И если бы за ним следом не пошёл, заблудился бы нафиг...
lines.uncensored: Ага, отнёс, блин! И если бы за ним следом не пошёл, заблудился бы на хрен...

notes: Translated line by line; the wife's reported order became her line. Three scenes: home, the forest where the cat walks off and the man stays lost, home again where the cat and then the unshaven man walk in. 'на хрен' rendered as a mild 'as hell', no softening needed.
title: The Cat in the Forest

lines.text: A man had a cat. Either the old tomcat had got too old, or he had stolen the sour cream, but the man's wife ordered:
Take him far into the forest and leave him there to his fate!
Nothing to be done, the man carried the cat into the forest.
And vanished himself.
One day he's gone, two days he's gone, on the third day the cat turns up at home,
and right behind it the man, dirty, angry and hungry.
Well, you moron, did you take the cat to the forest?
Yeah, I took him, damn it! And if I hadn't followed him back, I'd have been lost as hell...

notes: Translated line by line; the wife's reported order became her line. Three scenes: home, the forest where the cat walks off and the man stays lost, home again where the cat and then the unshaven man walk in. Swearing kept at 'verdammt' level, no softening needed.
title: Der Kater im Wald

lines.text: Ein Mann hatte einen Kater. Ob der Kater schon zu alt geworden war oder ob er die saure Sahne geklaut hatte, jedenfalls befahl die Frau:
Bring ihn weit in den Wald und überlass ihn dort seinem Schicksal!
Nichts zu machen, der Mann trug den Kater in den Wald.
Und verschwand selbst.
Einen Tag ist er weg, zwei Tage, am dritten Tag taucht zu Hause der Kater auf,
und gleich hinterher der Mann, dreckig, wütend und hungrig.
Na, du Trottel, hast du den Kater in den Wald gebracht?
Ja, hab ich, verdammt! Und wenn ich ihm nicht hinterhergelaufen wäre, hätte ich mich zum Teufel noch mal verlaufen...
